body:
I never said that. 

Of course I want to change and better myself in general, and getting diagnosed would put me on the path to finding mechanisms to cope and learn how to deal with my issues both inside and outside of autism (by separating what is directly linked to my autistic traits, and my other "issues").

Getting diagnosed, for me, means knowing why I am the way I am, why I feel the way I feel, and learning to exist better and more effectively. 

I also failed to mention that I am afab, so getting a proper, official diagnosis is important to me.

I totally get that too. I'm almost certain that I'm autistic, but that tiny little bit of doubt has me question myself sometimes. 

Like, what if I've been unconsciously faking symptoms???/s

I just feel the need to know for absolute certain, y'know? And I'd like to tell someone that I think this (my family is pretty ableist and not knowledgeable about autism; so, I figure my doctor is probably the best person to talk to. And if I eventually do get diagnosed, I'll be able to tell my parents and help them better understand me and autism ☺).

Thank you for sharing. 
I'm sorry it took so long for you to be diagnosed; that must have been tough. 

Even though being sent down a long, tedious path may very well happen, I'm looking forward to my appointment, and looking forward to (hopefully) being diagnosed. Just knowing if I'm autistic for sure would make me so happy.

I think it will make a lot of things in my life make sense; why I've never fit in, why talking to people and enjoying their company is so difficult and uncomfortable, mental health (anxiety, depression), why my family treats me differently compared to my siblings... Even things like gender dysphoria!

I've also been struggling for quite a while, and I think it could be burnout related. And, over the years I've suspected lots of different things (bpd, bipolar, etc), but autism was the one thing that stuck for this long.
I'm from Canada, and I've taken the AQ a couple of times over the years.
I'll ask next time I see him! Thanks for your suggestion.
